name: Credit spreads
summary: High-yield spreads tight at 3.3% — no sign of a credit crunch
state: The US high-yield option-adjusted spread was 3.26% at the latest reading (29 Oct), well inside the 4% Watch line and little changed over the month. Lenders are not yet demanding a meaningful premium for corporate default risk despite higher rates and energy costs.
for_you: Companies can still borrow on easy terms. A sharp widening would be an early sign of stress spreading from energy into the wider economy.

sources.title: FRED — ICE BofA US High Yield OAS (BAMLH0A0HYM2)

why: High-yield spreads show how much lenders demand to fund weaker companies — an early warning of defaults and credit crunches.
drivers: Default expectations, risk appetite, rates, private-credit stress, fund outflows.

rubric.alert: HY OAS > 6.0%, or widened > 200bp in a month.
rubric.watch: HY OAS 4.0–6.0%, or widened > 100bp in a month.
